summary: Configured node1 to rotate `/var/log/inventory/app.log` daily, retain seven compressed rotations, and use `copytruncate` so open writers continue writing. Verified rotation behavior and persistence across a node reboot.
actions_performed: Validated and exercised an isolated forced rotation.
Proved an open writer continued writing after rotation.
Restarted node1 exactly once and verified full recovery with a changed boot ID.

evidence.requirement: Daily rotation with seven compressed archives
evidence.summary: The installed rule specifies `daily`, `rotate 7`, and `compress`; logrotate parsed it as a daily seven-rotation rule and created a gzip archive.
A writer held the original inode open across rotation. Its pre-rotation record was archived, and its post-rotation record appeared in the truncated current file on the same inode.
The logrotate timer was enabled and active before configuration and remained enabled, active, and scheduled after restart.
Captured healthy pre-restart state and boot ID, reboot acknowledgement, restart disconnection, changed boot ID, and recovered system, timer, configuration, current log, and valid compressed archive.
